title: Ordinary compactified etale scalar mate on local sheet generators
statement:
Let $e:U\to V$ be a separated etale morphism of finite type between Noetherian schemes (schemes with finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings), and choose a compactification $U\xrightarrow jW\xrightarrow rV$, with $j$ open and $r$ proper [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-etale-morphism] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings, and let $M$ be any constant-$A$ module sheaf on $U_{\rm et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. All tensors below are ordinary sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $R=A,B$ write $j_{!,R}$, $r_{*,R}$ and $e_{\Sigma!,R}$ for extension by zero, direct image and sheafified sum extension [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension]. Let $\nu_{R,N}:r_{*,R}j_{!,R}N\xrightarrow{\sim}e_{\Sigma!,R}N$ be the degree-zero sheet-component comparison of [lem-asd-etale-compact-support-normalization]. Put $C=j_{!,A}M$ and $M_B=M\otimes_A B$. Define
$$\pi_C:(r_{*,A}C)\otimes_A B\longrightarrow r_{*,B}(C\otimes_A B)$$
as the ordinary $r_B^*\dashv r_{*,B}$ adjunct of
$$r_B^*((r_{*,A}C)\otimes_A B)\cong(r_A^*r_{*,A}C)\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{A,C}\otimes1}C\otimes_A B,$$
using the ordinary scalar/pullback reassociation and the ordinary counit [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image-tensor-comparison]. Let $o_M:C\otimes_A B\xrightarrow{\sim}j_{!,B}M_B$ be the open tensor map restricting to the identity on $U$ [lem-coef-etale-open-tensor]. Then
$$\nu_{B,M_B}\circ r_{*,B}(o_M)\circ\pi_C\circ(\nu_{A,M}^{-1}\otimes1)=\rho_M,$$
where $\rho_M:(e_{\Sigma!,A}M)\otimes_A B\to e_{\Sigma!,B}M_B$ is the sheaf map induced on local lift-indexed finite-sum generators by
$$(x_s)_s\otimes b\longmapsto(x_s\otimes b)_s.$$
Here a lift $s:S\to U$ lies over an etale test scheme $S\to V$, $x_s\in M(S,s)$, and $b$ may be any local section of the constant ring sheaf $B_V$; its image on the right is restricted along the same lift. The equality is natural in $M$, commutes with etale restriction, and is an equality of $B$-linear sheaf morphisms. It includes empty sheet sets, the zero sheaf, and the zero coefficient ring. No flatness of $M$ or $B$ over $A$, and no globally split test scheme, is assumed.

proof.text: Factor every compactification into the functor of properly supported sections using the open, proper and composition clauses of properSupportSheafComposition. Its inclusion in direct image is sectionwise injective. For a finite compactification supplied by Zariski main theorem the graph comparison is invertible. The graph normalization makes the graph maps for the two compactifications agree after this injective inclusion. Cancel the inclusion and transport invertibility to the chosen compactification.

proof.text: Construct rho as the hom of the left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism between sum extension followed by scalar extension and scalar extension followed by sum extension, using the literal sum/restriction adjunctions. Their right adjoints agree definitionally, since literal restriction commutes with restriction of scalars. The unit identity of leftAdjointUniq gives the sum/scalar unit identity directly. Separately identify upperStarRestrictScalarsIsoSheaf with literal restriction/scalar commutation transported through upperStarIsoLocalizationRestriction, using restriction/coextension units and left-adjoint uniqueness; this computes the prescribed coefficient pullback.

source.place: Tags 0GKF and 0GL6; etale-cohomology.tex Tags 03S5 and 0F4L; adjunction and graph normalization argument.

proof.text: Taking mates twice identifies the ordinary scalar/direct-image mate with the scalar-adjunction mate of the strict direct-image/restriction identity. Thus it preserves the scalar units. The open scalar comparison preserves the open units by its leftAdjointUniq definition. Transposing the open-to-direct map through the two geometric adjunctions and using their triangle identity proves compatibility with scalar units. Direct-image composition gives the same compatibility for compactificationSheafToDirectImage.

source.place: Tags 0GKF and 0GL6; etale-cohomology.tex Tags 03S5 and 0F4L; adjunction and graph normalization argument.

proof.text: The graph-extension unit commutes with restriction of coefficients by sheafCompose_map_lowerStarUnit_app, since restriction preserves zero morphisms. The literal sum/scalar unit identity therefore shows that rho commutes with the sum-to-direct map. Combine this with step 3 and the compactification graph normalization; cancel the sectionwise injective properly supported inclusion and transpose under the scalar adjunction. This identifies rho with the specified ordinary compactification composite.

proof.text: On local tensors, express scalarSheafTensorMap as the scalar unit followed by the B-sheaf tensor action. Naturality of the tensorator of sheafToPresheaf and its compatibility with sheafCompose prove this identity; restrictScalars_mu_tmul gives the elementary module balancing calculation. The literal restriction tensorator and its unit identify the action on arbitrary local coefficient sections after restriction along the chosen lift.

source.place: Tags 0GKF and 0GL6; etale-cohomology.tex Tags 03S5 and 0F4L; adjunction and graph normalization argument.

proof.text: Evaluate the literal sum/scalar unit identity at each test object and use projection_sum_unit to identify the result with etaleSumSection. The inverse-image/literal-restriction comparison identifies etaleLiftSection, and monoidality identifies compactificationCoefficientPullbackIso with the same coefficient restriction. Naturality of B-sheaf tensor action now proves the required local formula. All constructions are natural transformations, hence natural in M and compatible with restriction. Zero objects and empty sheets are covered by these same identities.
